title: The Hills That Rusted Rainbow — Zhangye Danxia · Silk Road EP4 | China Travel Expert
description:
Keep following the old Silk Road west across the Gobi and you reach one of the strangest sights in China: hills striped like a rainbow.

This is the Zhangye Danxia landform in Gansu, in the northern foothills of the Qilian Mountains. Its colors aren't paint — they're geology. Layers of sandstone and mineral, rich in iron, were laid down and then tilted by the same tectonic forces that lifted the Himalayas; as the iron slowly oxidised over roughly 24 million years, the rock turned bands of red, gold and blue, and wind and rain carved them into ridges. It was named a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2019.

🧭 Expert Tip: Aim to be on the boardwalks about an hour before sunset — low, warm light makes the mineral bands glow far more than harsh midday sun.
